input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: Since no historical actuals exist, I sized each backlog item in story points where given, and estimated points for "unestimated" items by comparing scope/complexity to similar estimated items. I then converted points to engineering hours using a baseline of ~6-8 hours per point (typical for small-medium teams with testing/review overhead), and split hours across roles based on the nature of each task (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, QA, infra/DevOps). I applied team capacity constraints (1.5 Backend FTE, 1.0 Frontend FTE, 0.6 QA FTE, 0.4 DevOps FTE) to sanity-check whether the allocated hours are deliverable in a reasonable timeframe (assumed ~3-4 month delivery window, i.e. ~13-17 weeks, giving each FTE roughly 500-650 available hours per role-FTE over the window).

Point-to-hour mapping used (blended across roles, before role-split): 1 point ≈ 7 hours of total engineering effort (dev+QA+devops combined), which is a common mid-range assumption for cross-functional teams delivering full-stack features including testing.

Estimated points for unestimated items (based on comparable complexity):
- PW-2 Design system: 13 (foundational, cross-cutting, used everywhere)
- PW-4 RBAC: 8 (matches similar security features like PW-17)
- PW-6 Invoice list/detail: 8 (similar to PW-5 dashboard)
- PW-8 Legacy data migration: 21 (large one-off ETL effort, high risk)
- PW-10 Audit log: 5
- PW-12 Support ticket submission: 5
- PW-14 Multi-currency: 13 (FX rates, settlement logic, display across currencies)
- PW-16 Performance hardening: 8 (profiling + indexing + caching)
- PW-18 Admin back-office: 8
- PW-20 Mobile responsive layout: 8 (cross-cutting UI work)
- PW-22 Observability: 8
- PW-24 Decommission legacy portal: 3 (mostly ops/config work)

Role split per task type:
- Auth/security/backend logic (PW-3,4,7,9,17,21): Backend-heavy with some Frontend + QA
- UI-heavy (PW-2,5,6,13,15,19,20): Frontend-heavy with Backend support + QA
- Infra/ops (PW-1,22,24): DevOps-heavy with Backend support
- Data (PW-8): Backend-heavy with QA validation
- Cross-cutting (PW-10,11,12,14,16,18,23): Mixed Backend/Frontend/QA

Total points estimated: 5+13+8+8+8+8+13+21+8+5+5+5+8+13+8+8+8+8+8+8+5+8+5+3 = 195 points
Total baseline hours = 195 * 7 ≈ 1365 hours total engineering effort across all roles.

I distributed this into role hours per the task-type splits, then checked against capacity: at ~4 months (17 weeks, ~68 hours/week per 1.0 FTE assuming 40hr/wk... actually using 40hr/wk standard), capacity over 4 months (~17 weeks) is:
- Backend: 1.5 FTE * 40 * 17 ≈ 1020 hours
- Frontend: 1.0 FTE * 40 * 17 ≈ 680 hours
- QA: 0.6 FTE * 40 * 17 ≈ 408 hours
- DevOps: 0.4 FTE * 40 * 17 ≈ 272 hours

My allocated hours (Backend 620, Frontend 460, QA 210, DevOps 130) fit within capacity comfortably, suggesting a ~3.5-4 month delivery timeline is feasible, though DevOps and QA are thinly staffed relative to the number of tasks touching them (e.g., PW-1, PW-7 webhooks, PW-8 migration validation, PW-22 all want DevOps/QA time) — flagged as an assumption/risk.

Priority breakdown was computed by summing the (hours*rate) cost of tasks grouped by priority label, using each task's role-cost allocation.

Scenarios: P50 (most likely, as estimated), P75 (+15% buffer for coordination/integration overhead across 24 tasks), P90 (+30% for realistic risk given migration, payments, and security items are inherently uncertain and QA/DevOps thinly staffed).

Reductions: identify concrete descope/defer opportunities among Low priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) and reducing scope of some Medium-priority "nice to have" items (PW-14 multi-currency, PW-16 performance hardening) or deferring them to a later phase.

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project; all estimates are derived from backlog scope and story points/comparisons only.
Unestimated backlog items were sized by analogy to similarly scoped estimated items (points assigned in reasoning).
Blended conversion rate of ~7 hours of total engineering effort per story point was used to translate points into hours, then split across roles by task nature.

Assumed a ~4 month (17-week) delivery window; role hour allocations were checked against each role's FTE capacity over that window and found feasible, though QA (0.6 FTE) and DevOps (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the number of tasks requiring their input (e.g. PW-1, PW-7, PW-8, PW-22), which is a schedule risk.
Backend Developer capacity (1.5 FTE) is assumed to also cover technical/architecture leadership given no separate Tech Lead role is staffed.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for third-party services/tooling (Stripe sandbox, cloud infra, accessibility audit, migration tooling) since no vendor quotes were provided.
Priority breakdown cost allocation approximates each task's role-hour cost and sums by its stated priority label; 'unestimated' points tasks are included using their assumed point values.
P75 and P90 scenarios add contingency for integration/coordination overhead and delivery risk (payments, data migration, thin QA/DevOps staffing) respectively, not for scope growth.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7) are treated as the highest technical risk items and are weighted heavily in the P90 scenario.

reductions.description: Descope or defer Low-priority items PW-12 (support ticket submission), PW-18 (admin back-office), PW-19 (usage analytics), PW-23 (contract tests), PW-24 (legacy decommission) to a later phase/backlog
reductions.effect: Removes ~5 low-priority tasks from current delivery scope, freeing Backend/Frontend/QA capacity for higher-priority urgent/high items

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) scope to a single settlement currency (USD) with display-only conversion for EUR/PLN, deferring full settlement logic
reductions.effect: Cuts backend/QA effort roughly in half for this feature by removing settlement reconciliation complexity

reductions.description: Defer Performance hardening of invoice list (PW-16) until real usage data shows it is needed, rather than building it speculatively
reductions.effect: Removes proactive backend/DevOps optimization work; revisit if p95 latency issues are observed in production

reductions.description: Use a managed/off-the-shelf accessibility audit tool instead of a full third-party WCAG audit, and have QA run automated checks
reductions.effect: Removes the non-labour third-party audit line item, shifting verification to existing QA capacity

reductions.description: Narrow Legacy data migration (PW-8) scope to a phased migration (most recent 12 months of invoice data first, historical data migrated later in background)
reductions.effect: Reduces initial migration engineering and QA validation effort by roughly 30%, deferring bulk historical migration to a follow-on project phase
